[process narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] TierPoint provides colocation, cloud, and managed IT services from a portfolio the company and its majority owner describe as roughly 40 data centers across about 18 to 20 U.S. markets. This session traced and dated the companys ownership structure, previously recorded without a clear citation chain: institutional investor Argo Infrastructure Partners began investing in TierPoint in 2020, added a further 500 million dollars in 2022, and took a majority stake by 2024. Per Argos own December 9, 2025 press release, Argo then acquired the equity interests of most of TierPoints remaining minority shareholders, consolidating its control and bringing total capital formation under Argos ownership to 3 billion dollars since 2020. Separately, per Data Center Dynamics trade press, Apollo Global Management announced in January 2025 that it would acquire Argo Infrastructure Partners itself, adding about 6 billion dollars in assets to Apollos infrastructure platform, with closing expected in the second quarter of 2025, meaning Argos majority stake in TierPoint now sits within Apollos broader infrastructure platform. This specific row, TierPoint Dallas-Allen, per the operators own dedicated page for this facility, fetched fresh this session, sits at 820 Allen Commerce Parkway, Allen, TX 75013, internally coded DA2, north of the main Dallas market.

reading.body:
This facility publishes no power capacity or rack count, so its scale relative to AI infrastructure investment cannot be assessed from its operator's spec page. TierPoint operates roughly 40 data centers across 18 to 20 U.S. markets as a colocation and managed services provider, now majority-owned by Argo Infrastructure Partners, which itself became part of Apollo Global Management's infrastructure platform in January 2025. The Dallas-Allen location sits north of the main Dallas market in Collin County.

Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities, of which 18 publish power capacity totaling 468 megawatts. This campus does not appear in that published inventory, placing it outside the ranked set of disclosed capacity in the state. Without a published megawatt figure from the operator, no comparison is possible to other Texas facilities or to AI scaling constraints in the region.

The absence of published specifications for this facility means it does not contribute to the publicly visible baseline of AI-relevant infrastructure capacity in Texas. If the facility hosts significant power and cooling, that capacity is not disclosed in operator marketing materials this site has indexed. Readers tracking grid-constrained AI deployment should note that most of TierPoint's portfolio similarly appears to publish no power specifications.
